prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in moiré flat-band matter.

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep B021 (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) as my single-part position. What I weigh most is a mechanism that is simple, analytically stated in advance and then tested: the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model of 2011 gives a magic angle from the competition between interlayer tunnelling and the Dirac velocity, and in 2018 the flat-band regime showed correlated insulators and superconductivity at exactly that angle. The central observation has since been reproduced by many independent groups with transport, scanning probes and spectroscopy, and it has opened a general platform (other moiré systems, tunable correlated and topological states). I distinguish between the discovery, which is established, and the explanation of the superconducting pairing, which is a follow-up question that does not change what was found. I considered a two-part prize with B024 but cannot build one inside the three-person limit without dropping a name that carries the B021 attribution (MacDonald and Bistritzer are the theory, Jarillo-Herrero the experiment), so I propose B021 alone.
statement.case_against: The weakest points are unchanged and I should state them plainly. The field is about eight years old, the pairing mechanism is open, and twist-angle disorder limits sample-to-sample comparison, so part of the headline physics is not yet understood, which matters to me. Round 1 also sharpened the maturity argument against me: B024 and B020 have roughly two decades of independent confirmation each. On attribution, Cao and the co-authors of the 2018 papers, and the parallel Dean, Yacoby and Young experiments, cannot be named, and I cannot say that Bistritzer's share is equal to MacDonald's; the two-name version Danielsson-Ulf floated is a defensible fallback but loses the 2011 co-author of the actual prediction. I also accept Olsson-Eva's point that a committee could reasonably wait a few years.

responses.point: Danielsson-Ulf prefers B025 as a decisive, fully mature observation, ranks B021 highly but young, and would accept a two-name B021 without Bistritzer; he also stresses that the BeppoSAX localisation and the ground-based optical and redshift credit cannot all fit in three names.
responses.response: I agree that B025 is the clearest observation-driven discovery on the list and that maturity there is beyond doubt. My difficulty is the attribution you yourself identify: the localisation credit and the optical afterglow and redshift credit are separable, van Paradijs is deceased and Groot and others fall outside, so three names may not honestly describe the discovery. On B021 I would keep Bistritzer: the 2011 paper is a two-author result, and dropping one of the two authors of the prediction to save a slot makes the theory half of the citation less accurate, not more. If the committee insists on two names I would accept MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, but I prefer the version where the prediction is credited as it was written.

responses.point: Kroll-Stefan prefers B024 as a new measurement capability that is reproduced across JILA, RIKEN, NIST, PTB and SYRTE, and concedes that the output so far is tighter limits, proximity to the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and an unmade redefinition of the second.
responses.response: I accept that B024 is the most reproduced and best-bounded candidate and I regard it as my main alternative, and your Katori-Ye attribution is cleaner than anything else on the shortlist. Where we differ is on what the prize should reward. A capability that has not yet produced a fact about nature beyond limits is, for me, a smaller step than a prediction followed by a new set of phases in matter. I am not persuaded by the argument that the maturity gap decides it, because B021 has already been replicated broadly, but I concede that your point about the pending redefinition cuts both ways: if the second is redefined, B024 becomes the stronger case and I would move it up. For now I rank it second.

responses.point: Olsson-Eva prefers B005 as a finished, verified discovery, calls B021 slightly early but defensible, and says the Moodera and Miyazaki 1995 observations are the original experiments while Parkin's credit rests on the later MgO step and the 2007 GMR prize sits close.
responses.response: I take the B005 case seriously as a verified experimental discovery with consequences outside the laboratory, and your insistence on who did the work first is a standard I share. My reservation is the one Eriksson-Olle raised and you quote: after 2007 a TMR prize reads as the device-oriented sequel, and a citation anchored on 1995 would have to leave Parkin and the MgO step out, which is where the technology actually moved. Since the attribution there is as unsettled as for B021, I do not see it as clearer than my proposal, and its theory (Butler, Mathon) is outside the names. On your question whether B021 is early: the flat-band and correlated-phase findings are replicated, and the open question is the pairing mechanism, which I treat as a follow-up.

responses.point: Lindroth-Eva prefers B020 (Bloch, Greiner, Zoller), argues that the Mott transition and single-site observation are themselves discoveries about how correlated quantum matter behaves, and notes that the doped Hubbard payoff is not yet in hand and that any three of five names leave out someone.
responses.response: You persuade me that the superfluid to Mott transition is a clean result about nature and not only a technique, and I have moved B020 into my alternatives. I do not move it to first place because the five-name credit is a real problem for me: choosing Zoller restores the theory proposal but drops Esslinger's fermionic work, while the experimental trio of Johansson-Goran drops the Jaksch-Zoller idea, and Cirac and Zoller also sit in B006. I think that is a sign that the discovery is a programme not yet condensed to one result, and the doped Hubbard model is the result that would condense it. If the committee does choose B020 I would favour the Bloch, Greiner, Zoller trio over the experimental trio, since the proposal is the mechanism.

responses.point: Eriksson-Olle also supports B021 as a clean prediction-and-observation pair and treats the correlated phases as established regardless of the pairing mechanism, while admitting that no second part could be built from the supplied names and that a two-name versus a three-name credit is open.
responses.response: I agree with you on the core of the argument, and your comparison with the 1987 high-temperature superconductivity prize is the right answer to the objection that the pairing must be settled first. I also agree that we cannot construct a satisfactory two-part version. One point I would add for the committee, since you ask about the three-name versus two-name choice: I prefer three, because with the 2011 paper credited to Bistritzer and MacDonald the prediction is attributed as written. I recognise that this uses the entire three-person budget on one achievement and leaves Cao and the parallel groups out, which we should acknowledge in the background text.

uncertainties: Whether members who regard the open pairing mechanism as a reason to wait will weigh B021 below B024 or B020 in the final vote; I think that is a legitimate position and cannot rule it out.
Whether the committee prefers three names for B021 or the two-name version without Bistritzer, and how to describe the contributions of Cao and the parallel experimental groups.
Whether the pending redefinition of the second would change my ranking of B024, which I currently rank as the main alternative.
Whether the credited names for B020 can be reduced to three that fairly describe the discovery, which affects whether it is my second alternative.
I rely on memory for the priority details around the 2011 prediction, the 2018 experiments and the parallel groups.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with the credited names of B021 or my alternatives; I have no collaboration, shared funding or institutional tie to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer, Katori, Ye or the B020 names. I work in the Gothenburg physics environment alongside Johansson-Goran and Olsson-Eva (Chalmers) without any specific collaboration, and I note that Johansson-Goran's flagged closeness to B002 no longer bears on the leading proposals.
